previous_statement: Let A,B >= 1 and k in (0,1/2] be universal witnesses from lem-stage1-approximate-group-laws, and let P >= 1 and q in (0,1/2] be universal witnesses from lem-stage1-polar-retraction. Set C_grp^0=A, C_pol^0=max(B,P), and kappa_pol^0=min(k,q). For every root instance, monotonicity of the nonnegative scalar expressions makes both external lemmas applicable. Write u_pol for the first component of the unique inverse of the explicit Pi_delta supplied by lem-stage1-polar-retraction, and u_grp for the function denoted u_delta by lem-stage1-approximate-group-laws. The retraction conclusions hold for u_pol, while the C^1 operations, identities, and A*epsilon_r estimates hold for u_grp. The registered contracts do not assert that u_grp is the first component of an inverse of that explicit Pi_delta, so uniqueness of Pi_delta's inverse does not imply u_grp=u_pol. Hence this branch proves the two conclusions only for separately named maps and does not prove every conclusion of node 1. A synchronized external statement, or a direct derivation that u_grp inverts the explicit Pi_delta with the required typing, remains necessary.
new_statement: Let A,B >= 1 and k in (0,1/2] be universal witnesses from lem-stage1-approximate-group-laws, and let P >= 1 and q in (0,1/2] be universal witnesses from lem-stage1-polar-retraction. Set C_grp^0=A, C_pol^0=max(B,P), and kappa_pol^0=min(k,q). For every root instance, monotonicity makes both external lemmas applicable. The retraction external supplies the explicit unique inverse (u_pol,h_pol), the group-laws external supplies all group conclusions for its polar inverse u_grp, and lem-stage1-polar-coherence-naturality identifies u_grp=u_pol because the two polar data have the same delta, source map, and image. Finally A<=C_grp weakens every A*epsilon_r estimate to the required C_grp*epsilon_r bound. Thus the arbitrary instance satisfies every root conclusion.
